lessons.title: Iolra lag: -án go -áin
lessons.rule: To make the plural of a noun ending in -án or -ún, put i before the final n: camán becomes camáin, botún becomes botúin.
steps: Find the noun in brackets: camán, which ends in -án.
Put i before the final n to make it slender: camáin.
Write it after na: Chuir muid na camáin isteach sa bhus i ndiaidh an chluiche iomána.

example.prompt: Chuir muid na (camán) isteach sa bhus i ndiaidh an chluiche iomána.
example.answer: Chuir muid na camáin isteach sa bhus i ndiaidh an chluiche iomána.

lessons.title: Iolra lag: caolú
lessons.en: Weak plural: make the last consonant slender
lessons.rule: For other first-declension nouns, put i after the last vowel so the final consonant is slender: crann becomes crainn, gasúr becomes gasúir. Where the last vowel is ea it changes to i (peann, pinn), and éa changes to éi (ticéad, ticéid).
steps: Find the last vowel in crann: a.
Put i after it so the nn becomes slender: crainn.
Write it after na: Tá na crainn ag cailleadh a gcuid duilleog san fhómhar.

example.prompt: Tá na (crann) ag cailleadh a gcuid duilleog san fhómhar.
example.answer: Tá na crainn ag cailleadh a gcuid duilleog san fhómhar.

more.prompt: Fág na (peann) ar an deasc roimh an scrúdú.
more.answer: Fág na pinn ar an deasc roimh an scrúdú.

lessons.hint: Put i after the last vowel; ea becomes i.

lessons.title: Na + guta: h roimh an iolra
lessons.en: After na, put h before a vowel
lessons.rule: Make the plural as usual; if it begins with a vowel, put h in front of it after na: oileán becomes na hoileáin, uan becomes na huain.
steps: Make the plural: oileán becomes oileáin.
It begins with a vowel, so put h in front of it after na: na hoileáin.
Write the sentence: Tá na hoileáin amach ó Thír Chonaill iontach ciúin sa gheimhreadh.

example.prompt: Tá na (oileán) amach ó Thír Chonaill iontach ciúin sa gheimhreadh.
example.answer: Tá na hoileáin amach ó Thír Chonaill iontach ciúin sa gheimhreadh.
